thread:
incident-bot: PAGING: Streaming latency SLO breach in us-west-2 — p99 > 2.5s for /v1/generate (streaming). Alerts from 1719456700.

jon (oncall): ACK. I'm on it. grabbing graphs now.

alex (runtime): seeing huge tail on streamer shards 3/7. p95 ~ 800ms -> 1.6s, p99 ~ 2.7s. Streaming stalls and chunking delays. Link: https://grafana/redwood/streams?from=1719456600

maria (ml-infra): correlating with the prompt-template rollout 2024-06-09T03:40 (feature flag: prompt-json-mode=true). We enabled JSON-mode preproc that expands tool schemas inline. Hypothesis: tokenizer is doing extra work per-request (reserializing, escaping).

nina (cust-success): got 3 customer escalations in last 10m; one reported partial stream (truncated JSON) then connection closed. Customer: AcmePayments. They hit rate ~200rps.

sam (eng-sre): first mitigation: route streaming traffic to non-streaming fallback or lower-tokenized model for heavy users, and scale dedicated pools. Can someone flip routing quickly?

alex (runtime): I can change routing policy. Proposing: 1) toggle prompt-json-mode off via FF, 2) re-route top 5 heavy orgs to dedicated pool, 3) scale streamer replicas x2. Doing (1) now.

alex (runtime): Command I used: `curl -X POST https://flags.internal/flags/prompt-json-mode/toggle -d '{"value": false}'`

devops-bot: Feature flag prompt-json-mode set to false by alex at 1719456881.

jon (oncall): nice. After FF toggle, metrics?

alex (runtime): rerouted 3 heavy orgs (AcmePayments, NovaForms, QuickHR) to dedicated pools and bumped streamer replicas: `kubectl scale deployment/streamer --replicas=14 -n us-west-2`.

sam (eng-sre): also restarted tokenizer worker pool to flush any stuck workers: `./ops/restart_service tokenizer-worker --region us-west-2`

maria (ml-infra): adding more detail — the JSON-mode path was doing an extra pass that expands tool schema placeholders like `{{tool_schema}}` into full JSON doc for each call, and then runs `json.dumps` style escaping. That adds ~100-400 tokens per request for tools-heavy prompts, which exacerbates batching inefficiency and KV cache utilization.

alex (runtime): after changes, p95 dropped back to ~600ms and p99 ~1.1s for streaming in us-west-2. Still seeing occasional stalls (~0.5% requests).

nina (cust-success): letting AcmePayments know we mitigated and we've routed them to dedicated capacity. They asked for ETA on permanent fix.

jon (oncall): good. Action items: - rollback template expansion in code (maria) - add protective cap in preproc to avoid full schema expansion (maria) - better feature-flag safety tests (devx) - postmortem + customer-impact summary (nina). I'll handoff to maria at next step.

maria (ml-infra): I've pushed a quick-change to revert expansion and added a guard: if estimated token growth > 30% skip full expansion and leave placeholders. Patch: `revert-expansion-20240609` pushed to canary.

devops-bot: Deploy started for revert-expansion-20240609 -> canary at 1719457420.

alex (runtime): canary looks clean. Spikes on the canary host are gone. Scheduling roll to prod in 5m.

sam (eng-sre): reminder: we also need traces. Please capture a couple of full request traces for p99 cases. Use `curl -H "X-Debug-Trace:1"` and attach to Sentry.

maria (ml-infra): captured traces, attaching summary link: https://traces.internal/trace/abcd1234. Note tokenizer CPU flatlined during spike. Gonna investigate library version and whether version bump changed tokenization strategy.

jon (oncall): customer-impact estimate?

nina (cust-success): 6 customers impacted, highest severity AcmePayments (partial outputs, retries). Estimated MTTI ~22m, we notified all 6 within 15m of detection. One support ticket escalated to SE.

alex (runtime): post rollback and scale, streaming error rate dropped from 2.1% -> 0.08% over 10m.

sam (eng-sre): good. Keep the ded pool routing until we confirm no regressions. Also temporarily increase tokenization worker autoscale thresholds.

maria (ml-infra): root cause (prelim): prompt-json-mode enabled a code path that serializes tool schemas into prompt at request time which ballooned token counts and triggered inefficient batching + KV cache misses leading to higher tail latency. Also noticed a tokenizer library minor version change in last upgrade that slightly changed byte-to-token heuristics (makes worst-case token count larger).

jon (oncall): OK. Next steps: - maria to revert in prod (DONE) - alex to keep routing for heavy orgs for 2 hours - sam to monitor streamer tail for next 4 hours - nina to update customers with RCA once postmortem is ready - create postmortem ticket and link traces (jon)

jon (oncall): i'm handing off oncall to alex for monitoring window. alex, you own the incident for the next 4 hours. I'm OOO after 1719460000.

alex (runtime): taking over. I'll keep watch and post updates.

nina (cust-success): prepping customer-impact note for AcmePayments and NovaForms. Will include mitigation steps and ETA for permanent fix.

sam (eng-sre): follow-ups: - add unit/integration tests for FF to catch token growth > X% - add synthetic load tests that exercise tool-schema expansion path - consider adding a static precompute step for tool schemas at model-load time, not per-request.

maria (ml-infra): agreed. I'll open a tech task for static precompute and for auditing tokenizer library versions across clusters.

jon (oncall): thanks team. Updating incident-bot to resolved for now once metrics stabilize. Will open postmortem ticket and assign owners. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident 2024-06-09-1719456789 status: mitigated -> monitoring.

alex (runtime): monitoring shows steady state. I'll mark resolved after 2h if no regressions.

nina (cust-success): sending customer update now.

sam (eng-sre): leaving a note: if you see streaming stalls with sudden token count jumps, check prompt-template FF and tokenizer-worker CPU.

maria (ml-infra): filing follow-up PRs and will attach perf regression tests.

jon (oncall): handoff complete.
